jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, Dallas

headline: Fourteen Indicted in Alleged $370 Million Bank-Account-Takeover Ring Featuring Corrupt Bank and Telecom Insiders
deck: Federal prosecutors in Dallas unsealed a 22-count indictment accusing Muhamed Dieye—allegedly known as ‘Medici’ and ‘Lambomotion Tony’—and 13 co-defendants of targeting nearly 3,000 victims’ accounts across major U.S. banks. All defendants are presumed innocent.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Federal grand jury in Dallas indicted 14 defendants in a 22-count indictment alleging a nationwide bank-account-takeover conspiracy targeting nearly 3,000 victims with over $370M in combined account balances using SIM swaps and alleged insiders at major banks and telecom carriers; defendants presumed innocent.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: If proven, the allegations would resemble bribing a neighborhood bank teller and locksmith to copy safe-deposit keys for 3,000 customers at once
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate felony arrest warrants and mandatory consecutive aggravated identity-theft enhancements

sources.title: Federal Grand Jury Indicts Fourteen Defendants in $370 Million Nationwide Bank-Account-Takeover Conspiracy

interactive_art_spec.caption: Classical limestone facade of the 1920 Federal Reserve Bank building in Dallas. Federal prosecutors in the Northern District of Texas unsealed a 22-count indictment charging 14 defendants in an alleged $370 million nationwide bank-account-takeover conspiracy.
